name: Austrian Empire

areaKm2.note: world_1815 polygon "Austrian Empire" = 605,200 km2 on the sphere. The 1866 monarchy (without Lombardy, lost 1859, with Venetia until October 1866) was ~650,000 km2; Austrian Empire page infobox gives 698,700 km2 for the pre-1859 empire.

population.note: COW NMC v7 tpop: 1865 = 37,004k, 1866 = 34,482k (annual value after the cession of Venetia, ~2.5M). In June 1866 Venetia was still Austrian, so mid sits between.

urbanization.note: HYDE (OWID) 1860/1870: Austria 23%/26%, Czechia 15%/17%, Hungary 10%/12%; Galicia and the Balkan lands lower. COW upop 1866 = 1,122k (cities 100k+) = 3%.

activePersonnel.note: Austro-Prussian War infobox: Austria 407,223 deployed (Clodfelter 2017 p. 183). Nordarmee ~240,000 incl. Saxons (Koeniggraetz page: 184,000 Austrians and 22,000 Saxons at the battle), Suedarmee ~75,000, garrisons. COW milper 1865 = 300,000 is a peacetime annual value.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess: depot (Ersatz) battalions and recalled reservists still forming in June-July 1866; Austria had no Landwehr comparable to Prussia's.

supportPersonnel.note: Artillery ~25,000, engineers and pioneers ~5,000, train ~10,000, navy ~10,000 (Tegetthoff's fleet). Reconstruction.

mobilizationRatio.note: Educated guess: Austria mobilised ~1.2% of its population in 1866; a total effort on the later Austro-Hungarian system reached ~6% in 1914.

mobilizable.note: population x mobilizationRatio (low x low, mid x mid, high x high).

count.note: 80 line regiments on war footing (many at low strength after furloughs); share of the 407,223 total after cavalry, artillery and support.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Lorenz rifled muzzle-loader against the Dreyse breech-loader

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5. Evidence: Stosstaktik bayonet doctrine, little musketry; long nominal service with long furloughs

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: Lorenz rifles and jaeger carbines

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.5-0.75. Evidence: jaeger marksmanship better than the line

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: good horses

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: won the cavalry clash at Strezetitz after Koeniggraetz

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: Hungarian hussars

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: well trained, poorly used for reconnaissance

count.note: Field guns: Nordarmee ~770 (Wawro, isbn:0-521-56059-4, ch. 9), Suedarmee ~160, reserves. The Koeniggraetz page records 187 Austrian guns lost in that battle alone.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.75. Evidence: M1863 rifled muzzle-loaders (Lenk system) outranged half the Prussian smoothbores (Austro-Prussian War page)

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: the army reserve artillery covered the retreat at Koeniggraetz

count.note: Lissa order of battle: 4 ironclads + 3 armoured frigates (7 armoured ships), 1 ship of the line (Kaiser) and 5 screw frigates = 13. A few more units were not at Lissa.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: smaller, weaker-armed ironclads than Italy's

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: Tegetthoff drilled ramming tactics; beat a larger fleet at Lissa

count.note: At Lissa: 1 screw corvette, 2 screw gunboats, 6 gunboats, tenders; plus Venetian lagoon and Danube flotillas.

quality.note: Rubric row: quality 0.5. Evidence: small screw gunboats

training.note: Rubric row: training 0.75. Evidence: Tegetthoff's crews

commandQuality.note: Rubric row: commandQuality 0.25-0.5. Evidence: Benedek at Koeniggraetz, no general staff on the Prussian model; Archduke Albrecht won Custoza in Italy

cohesion.note: Rubric row: cohesion 0.5. Evidence: multi-national army; Italian and Hungarian units unreliable

morale.note: Rubric row: morale 0.5. Evidence: defeat of 1859; Custoza and Lissa in 1866

weapons.note: Anchor: between 6 (1805) and 7 (1905). Evidence: rifled muzzle-loading infantry and artillery, no breech-loader

armor.note: Anchor: 6 (none / cuirass). Evidence: cuirassiers only; no land armour

ships.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: broadside ironclads (Drache, Kaiser Max class) and a converted wooden ship of the line

fortification.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: Quadrilateral (Verona, Peschiera, Mantua, Legnago), Olmuetz, Josefstadt

logistics.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: Moltke: Austria had one railway line north and needed 45 days to assemble 200,000 men (Austro-Prussian War page)

communications.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: electric telegraph to army headquarters

isr.note: Anchor: between 6 and 7. Evidence: cavalry screens poorly used

air.note: No military aircraft before 1911; balloons, where used, are counted under ISR.

gdpPerCapita.note: Maddison Project 2023 (OWID): Austria (modern borders) 1860 = 2,834, 1870 = 2,970; Hungary 1870 = 1,741; Italy 1866 = 2,588 (Venetia); Galicia and the Balkan lands far poorer. Population-weighted monarchy ~2,000.

gdp.note: population x gdpPerCapita (low x low, mid x mid, high x high), 2011 int$.

milSpendShare.note: COW NMC v7 milex (thousands of pounds): 1865 = 9,121, 1866 = 22,756. Against a national product of roughly 300-350M pounds that is ~3% in peace and ~7% in the war year.

industrialShare.note: Educated guess: industry concentrated in Bohemia and Lower Austria.

annualCohort.note: Analogue: France 1805 snapshot ratio, males reaching military age = 0.95-1.15% of population per year (Elting ch. 9), applied to this population.

artillery.note: Educated guess: Vienna Arsenal field-gun output per year.

ships_major.note: Educated guess: ironclads launched per year at Trieste (Stabilimento Tecnico) and Pola.

roadKm.note: Educated guess: Reichsstrassen and provincial engineered roads.

railKm.note: CHAT (https://data.nber.org/chat/chat.dta) railline Austria 1866 = 3,965 km; Hungarian network ~2,200 km in 1866 (educated estimate, CHAT has no Hungary value); Venetian lines small.

majorPorts.note: Educated guess: Trieste, Venice, Pola, Fiume, Zara, Spalato.

merchantTonnage.note: Registered merchant tonnage 306k tons (Austria 1866, CHAT dataset https://data.nber.org/chat/chat.dta, variable shipton_all) x 1.5 (range 1.3-1.6). CHAT tonnage is registered (largely net) tons, so this may understate deadweight.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess: rail to Bohemia, then wagons.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess: horses of the monarchy; Hungary a major horse breeder.

homeDefense.note: 1.1-1.2 rows: familiar terrain, fortress system in Italy and Moravia; mixed population support.

notes: Snapshot = Austrian Empire in mid-June 1866 on war footing (Seven Weeks War). Territory and population incl. Venetia (ceded October 1866) and Hungary; German Confederation allies (Saxony 26,500, Bavaria 38,000, Hanover 18,400 etc.) excluded; includes is empty. Personnel: mobilised army and navy = active; depot battalions and further reservists = trainedReserves. Strengths from the Austro-Prussian War page (Clodfelter 2017 p. 183), Koeniggraetz page and Lissa page; branch split is a reconstruction (grade C).
